audit.why: 25% over 12 games is the worst matchup in Akshan's slice, and the chart correctly gives Tryndamere everything from level 3 onward except the level-6 stage. The prose already treats this as a lane to survive, not win.
Lvl 2-3 as Akshan's only window, Lvl 6 Undying Rage as the hard counter, the first-item race Akshan loses, and Tryndamere's crit scaling. All four correctly placed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Mocking Shout as an unconditional slow that stops you kiting — 'W-slow you so you can't kite the spin', 'E + W break my Q rhythm and slow me out of position'. The slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' That conditional is the single most useful piece of information in this matchup for a champion trying to escape a gap-close: retreat while facing him and you keep full move speed, turning a guaranteed catch into a survivable one. The page instead taught the reader that the slow is automatic and disengage is hopeless.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (W, 850 range, 14s) always cuts your AD, but it only slows you if your back is turned — back away facing him and you keep your speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on Spinning Slash or Bloodlust.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8s and 650 range — that is the number that defines how far you must stand from him. Bloodlust is 12s flat, which sets how often his Fury converts to health.
audit.corrected: E 12s at rank 1, 650 range; Q 12s flat.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing despite the whole entry being about his sustain.
audit.why: Bloodlust converts the Fury bar directly into health every 12s. Grievous Wounds is the itemisation lever and it was never named.

audit.whatIsWrong: This entire entry is written in the first person — 'I get exactly one job', 'my Avengerang', 'I own these levels' — across early, mid, late and all seven whys. Every other Akshan matchup addresses the reader as 'you'.
audit.why: The approved quality bar is the user's second-person voice. A single first-person page reads as a different author and breaks the loading-screen format the site uses everywhere else.
audit.corrected: Converted to second person throughout the strings I touched.

edits.after: Stack Fury for crit and Bloodlust heals, then Spinning Slash in — Mocking Shout only slows you once you turn

edits.before: I get exactly one job early: abuse levels 2-3 before his crit shows up. Avengerang (Q) out-ranges his autos, so chip him while his Fury bar is empty, his crit chance is floored, and his lifesteal is nothing. The trap is his E (Spinning Slash) — the second I step up to auto and proc my second shot, he can E-gap onto me, W-slow me so I can't kite, and start spinning. Last-hit at max Q range, never walk up to CS, and respect that a Fury-stacked Trynd at half health is more dangerous than a full one, because his crit chance and self-heal both scale with the bar.
edits.after: You get exactly one job early: abuse levels 2-3 before his crit shows up. Avengerang (Q) out-ranges his autos, so chip him while his Fury bar is empty, his crit chance is floored, and his lifesteal is nothing. The trap is Spinning Slash (E) — 650 range on a 12s cooldown, and it lands the moment you step up to proc your second shot. Mocking Shout only slows enemies with their BACKS TURNED, so retreat facing him and you keep full speed. Last-hit at max Q range, and respect a wounded Trynd: Bloodlust scales his AD with missing health.

edits.before: This is where it slips away. At 6 his Undying Rage (R) answers my entire kit — I'm a pick/execute champ, and he literally cannot die for 5 seconds, so my Comeuppance (R), my second-shot burst, and my E-reset-on-takedown snowball all hit a wall. If I commit my combo and he ults, I've blown everything and he spins me down with a full Fury bar. Don't all-in him at 6. Keep E to swing away when he E's onto me, hold R for a ranged poke finish or a roam pick, and make plays in other lanes with W camouflage instead of feeding him a 1v1 he survives by design.
edits.after: This is where it slips away. Commit the combo and he ults, and he spins you down with a full Fury bar. Don't all-in him at 6. Keep E to swing away when he gaps in, hold R for a ranged poke finish or a roam pick, and make plays in other lanes with W camouflage instead of feeding him a 1v1 he survives by design.

edits.before: He hard out-scales me and there's no pretending otherwise. Crit Trynd spin-kites, his E + W break my Q rhythm and slow me out of position, and Undying Rage means even a perfect Comeuppance + E setup just leaves him at 1 HP before he turns and kills me. My lethality damage falls off against his crit-and-sustain statline. My only path is to have already snowballed off levels 2-5, then play the map — pick squishies with R, group, and let my team peel — because I lose every late 1v1 to him.
edits.after: He hard out-scales you and there's no pretending otherwise. Crit Trynd spin-kites, and Undying Rage means even a perfect Comeuppance setup just leaves him alive before he turns and kills you. Bloodlust converts his Fury bar straight into health every 12s, so Grievous Wounds is the only itemisation that touches the problem — and alone it still isn't enough. Your path is to have snowballed off levels 2-5, then play the map: pick squishies with R, group, and let your team peel, because you lose every late 1v1.

notes: Two things. First, Mocking Shout's slow is conditional on your back being turned — the page presented it as unconditional and told the reader kiting was impossible. Backing away while facing Tryndamere keeps your move speed, which is the difference between escaping a Spinning Slash and dying to one. Second, this was the only Akshan entry written in the first person ('I get exactly one job', 'my Avengerang'); I converted every string I touched to the site's second-person voice. The packet's suspectName flag on whys[1] ('My Avengerang') was a FALSE POSITIVE — Avengerang is correct and the detector tripped on the preceding word. I did not add any duration claim for Undying Rage; the existing '5 seconds' text sits in strings I rewrote and I dropped rather than repeated it, since Riot's description states no duration.
